narrativeProgression.description: The speaker highlights the interconnected nature of global economies in the present day.
The speaker introduces the concept of "strong headwinds," which represent challenges to global economic integration.
The speaker suggests that these challenges include nationalist trade policies and protectionist pressures.
Unilateral solutions, according to the speaker, are ineffective in addressing these challenges.
International trade is positioned as a vital component of positive economic growth.
The speaker emphasizes the need for growth to be of good quality, sustainable, and inclusive.
Leveraging the positive aspects of digitalization technology is presented as one way to achieve these growth goals.
The speaker highlights the often-overlooked aspect of mitigating the negative impacts of technological advancements.
Managing the transition brought about by technological progress is crucial.
The speaker stresses the importance of preventing societal divisions both within and between countries.
The speaker believes that these two dimensions - open markets and effective redistribution mechanisms - are paramount in today's economic climate.
The speaker underscores the need to maintain open markets while acknowledging the necessity of robust redistribution systems within countries to ensure equitable outcomes.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: How do you deal with the problem?
Our economies are today much more interrelated.
There are lots of strong headwinds that are pushing in a different direction,
that maybe are pushing for more nationalistic trade policies,
that are pushing for more trade protection, these pressures.
Unilateral solutions, we think, is not going to work.
International trade is a very important piece of good quality growth,
sustainable growth, inclusive growth.
This requires both leveraging the positive force
that digitalisation technology can have,
but also, and this is the part that maybe we haven't thought enough,
mitigating the impact of technological progress.
And I think the key will be in how we manage the transition.
How do we make sure that we don't have divides within societies
and we do not have divides among countries?
This two-dimensions must be central to what I think it did.
We have to maintain markets open,
but also not forget that for open markets to work,
there are distribution mechanisms at home have to be much stronger,
to maintain more harmonious trade and investment relations.

youtube_description:
Global Future Councils on the Future of International Trade and Investment

This Council explores the future of the international trade and investment system and provides thought leadership to high-level policy fora such as the G20 and Asia Pacific Economic Forum (APEC)

Focus areas include:  
- International trade as a vehicle for sustainable development 
- Role of investment, trade and competition policies in regional integration processes 
- Digital economy and its impact on economic growth and inclusiveness 
- Developments in the global production and supply chains, shaped by the Fourth Industrial Revolution 
- Practical reforms to facilitate the flow of goods through customs and across borders
